math_exp_02.description: English-reading secondary-school learner with the listed geometry prerequisites. Report only what the video supports.

known.K0: A triangle has three vertices and interior angles.
known.K2: Rigid translation and rotation preserve an angle's measure.
known.K3: Corresponding and alternate interior angles for parallel lines.

not_assumed: A proof or general explanation of the triangle angle-sum result.

math_exp_02.description: English-reading learner beginning angle geometry; a fixed prerequisite hypothesis, not a requirement to be confused.

known.K1: Angles can be compared and measured in degrees.

not_assumed: Why moving or rotating an angle preserves its measure.
A proof of the triangle angle-sum result.

math_prob_01.description: English-reading learner beginning worked linear-equation examples, with the listed arithmetic and equality prerequisites.

known.K0: Integer addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
known.K1: A letter can stand for an unknown number; 2x means twice x.
known.K2: Applying the same addition, subtraction or nonzero division to both sides preserves equality.

not_assumed: The solution or step sequence for this particular equation.

math_prob_01.description: English-reading arithmetic learner new to algebraic equality transformations; do not force confusion when the video explains them.

known.K0: Integer addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
known.K1: An equals sign says the two numerical values are the same.
known.K2: A letter can represent an unknown number.

not_assumed: Why the same operation is applied to both sides of an equation.
The convention that 2x means twice x.
